description: The Metal Rat in Chinese astrology: personality, Metal element traits, 1960 and 2020 dates and compatibility.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Metal Rat is the Rat born in a Metal year, one of five versions of the first animal. It combines the Rat's quick wits with Metal's qualities. Metal Rat years between 1924 and 2044 are 1960 and 2020. The Rat's fixed element is Water.

sections.heading: The Metal Rat personality
paragraphs: With a Metal stem, the Rat's sharp wits acquire an edge of determination. Metal generates Water in the five-element cycle, and the Rat's fixed element is Water, so the year element is traditionally said to strengthen and supply the animal rather than challenge it. Metal Rats are often described as ambitious, disciplined and persuasive, able to set a goal and pursue it with unusual tenacity. They tend to have refined tastes, strong opinions and a clear sense of what they want from life. The doubled resourcefulness can make them excellent with money and planning. The flip side, according to many readings, is a hard shell: Metal Rats may guard their feelings carefully and become stubborn once a decision is made.

Metal is the element of autumn and harvest, and a Metal year is traditionally said to sharpen whatever animal it meets. Descriptions associate it with determination, discipline, clear judgement and a strong code of principle. Metal-year people are often portrayed as decisive, self-reliant and willing to do difficult things because they are right. The element is linked with refinement and with cutting away what is unnecessary, so it tends to bring focus and high standards. Its traditional shadow is rigidity: Metal can become inflexible, proud or emotionally guarded, preferring to be correct over being close, and finding it hard to bend once a position is taken.

sections.heading: Metal Rat at work and in love
paragraphs: At work, Metal is usually linked with discipline, precision and principled leadership. Metal-year people are often described as the ones who set standards, cut through confusion and finish what they start, which suits law, engineering, finance, surgery, editing and any role that values exactness. They tend to work well alone and lead by example. The traditional caution is inflexibility: a Metal stem can dismiss ideas that arrive untidily, so practising curiosity before judgement usually makes them better leaders.

The Metal Rat often treats a career like a campaign, complete with targets, milestones and a clear-eyed view of the competition. Traditional accounts match it with finance, law, consultancy, engineering management and any setting where sharp analysis must end in a firm recommendation. Autonomy and measurable goals bring out its best; vague leadership irritates it. As a partner it is protective and exacting, determined to secure a comfortable future for the people it loves. Ideally it pairs with someone who has ambitions of their own and the nerve to disagree out loud. The rub is inflexibility: a Metal Rat may defend its plan long after circumstances have changed, leaving the other person feeling overruled rather than consulted.

sections.heading: Metal Rat years and dates
paragraphs: Between 1924 and 2044 the Metal Rat years are 1960 (January 28, 1960 to February 14, 1961) and 2020 (January 25, 2020 to February 11, 2021). Because the year begins at Lunar New Year, a birthday in January or early February needs checking: in 1960 anyone born before Jan 28 is a Earth Pig, not a Metal Rat. The combination returns every sixty years, since five elements cycle through twelve animals and only meet the same pairing again after five rounds of the zodiac. Every Metal Rat year is Yang, matching the Rat's own polarity.

Chinese almanacs call the combination Geng-Zi, joining the heavenly stem Geng to the earthly branch Zi. Births just before each new year fall in the Earth Pig year (before January 28, 1960) and the Earth Pig year (before January 25, 2020), and births in the weeks after each Metal Rat year ends belong to the Metal Ox. The new year itself fell on a Thursday in 1960 and Saturday in 2020.

sections.heading: Growth edges and compatibility for the Metal Rat
paragraphs: For the Metal Rat, the growth edge usually involves softness and flexibility. Readings often suggest that this combination can mistake rigidity for strength, so practising open questions before stating a view is a useful habit. Metal Rats may also chase success so steadily that rest and relationships slip down the list; scheduling unstructured time with people they love tends to correct that. Because Metal and Water both favour inner reserve, sharing a worry with a trusted friend can feel uncomfortable but brings real relief. When the Metal Rat lets warmth soften its focus, its loyalty and capability become far easier for others to see and appreciate.

For relationships, the classical structures belong to the animal rather than the element, so the Metal Rat shares the Rat's San He trine with the Dragon and Monkey (the Water trine), its Liu He bond with the Ox, and its Liu Chong clash with the Horse. The element adds a second layer: another Metal sign shares this year element, while partners whose year element feeds Metal in the generating cycle are often described as supportive.

faq.question: What years are Metal Rat years?
faq.answer: Between 1924 and 2044: 1960 (from January 28, 1960) and 2020 (from January 25, 2020). Each lasts until the day before the next Lunar New Year.

faq.question: What is the Metal Rat's element relationship?
faq.answer: The year element is Metal and the Rat's fixed element is Water; in the five-element cycles metal generates Water. Readings use that relationship to describe how easily the two sides of the sign sit together.

faq.question: Which animals are most compatible with the Metal Rat?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Dragon and Monkey (San He) and the Ox (Liu He). The Horse is the Liu Chong clash. These pairings depend on the animal, whatever the element.

faq.question: What is the Metal Rat called in the Chinese calendar?
faq.answer: Geng-Zi. In almanacs and Four Pillars charts each year is named by its heavenly stem, here the Metal stem Geng, followed by its earthly branch, here Zi for the Rat, so the name pins down both halves of the combination at once.

faq.question: How is the Metal Rat different from other Rats?
faq.answer: All Rats share quick wits, resourcefulness and adaptability. The Metal year element changes the tone: metal is the element of autumn and harvest, and a Metal year is traditionally said to sharpen whatever animal it meets.
